newsitem.title: GERMANY: Albania force could need second mandate - minister.
newsitem.headline: Albania force could need second mandate - minister.

text.p: Albanian Foreign Minister Arjan Starova said on Friday an Italian-led multinational force to secure aid to his chaotic country would need a new mandate to stay on if planned elections did not go ahead in June.

But Starova told journalists in Bonn a postponement of elections was unlikely because Albania was gradually returning to normal after the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes triggered an armed insurrection.

After talks with German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, Starova said the Albanian authorities fully supported a mission to Albania by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), and were committed to elections at the end of June.
"Very soon the public (order) will come to normal order and if it reaches this level (there will be) no obstacle for free and fair elections in Albania," Starova said, in comments made in English.

"Foreign troops will stay in Albania...until the elections. If the elections are postponed, which I do not think is likely, of course the multinational protection force will need a second mandate," he said.

Nearly 300 people have been killed and about 700 hurt in an armed uprising over the last six weeks since the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes in which many Albanians lost their life savings.
An Italian-led 6,000-strong multinational force started arriving two weeks ago on a mission to safeguard emergency food and medicine supplies.
Kinkel said the security situation in Albania had calmed down but parts of the country remained unstable.
